post.summary: If a check-in was made in error and the person was not let in, it can be annulled
post.description:
If a check-in was made in error and the person was not let in, it can be annulled. We do not recommend this to be used in case of manual check-ins or user interfaces because it is too prone for human errors. It is mostly intended for automated entry systems like a turnstile or automated door, where the check-in is first created, then the door is opened, and then the check-in may be annulled if the system knows that the turnstile did not turn or was out of order.

This endpoint supports passing multiple check-in lists for the context of a multi-event scan. However, each check-in list passed needs to be from a distinct event.

Check-ins created by a device can only be annulled by the same device. The datetime of annulment may not be more than 15 minutes after the datetime of check-in (value subject to change).

A status code of 404 is returned if no check-in was found for the given nonce. A status code of 400 is returned when multiple check-ins match the nonce, the input is invalid in another way, the annulment is made from the wrong device, the check-in is already in an annulled or failed state, or the datetime constraint is not valid.

parameters.name: organizer
parameters.description: The `slug` field of the organizer to fetch

datetime.description: Specifies the client-side datetime of the annulment. If not supplied, the current time will be used.

400.description: Invalid or incomplete request, see above

404.description: The requested nonce does not exist.

post.summary: Tries to redeem an order position, i.e. checks the attendee in (or out)
post.description:
Tries to redeem an order position, i.e. checks the attendee in (or out). This is the recommended endpoint to use if you build any kind of scanning app that performs check-ins for scanned barcodes. It is safe to use with untrusted inputs in the `secret` field.

This endpoint supports passing multiple check-in lists to perform a multi-event scan. However, each check-in list passed needs to be from a distinct event.

parameters.name: expand

type.description: Send `"exit"` for an exit and `"entry"` (default) for an entry.

exchange_medium_type.description: To perform an exchange to a reusable medium, pass the type of the new reusable medium

exchange_medium_identifier.description: To perform an exchange to a reusable media, pass the identifier of the new medium

use_order_locale.description: Specifies that pretix should use the customer's language (`locale` field from the order) when building texts (currently only the `reason_explanation` response field). Defaults to `false` in which case the server will determine the language (currently the event default language, might change in the future with support for the `Accept-Language` header).

simulate.description: Do not actually perform the check-in, only simulate the response. The `position` response object will not reflect the simulated changes.

get.summary: Returns a list of all order positions matching a given search request
get.description:
Returns a list of all order positions matching a given search request. The result is the same as the order-position-resource, with the following differences:
- The `checkins` value will only include check-ins for the selected list.
- An additional boolean property `require_attention` will inform you whether either the order or the item have the `checkin_attention` flag set.
- If `attendee_name` is empty, it will automatically fall back to values from a parent product or from invoice addresses.

This endpoint supports passing multiple check-in lists to perform a multi-event search. However, each check-in list passed needs to be from a distinct event.

parameters.description: Fuzzy search matching the attendee name, order code, invoice address name as well as to the beginning of the secret.

post.description:
Creates a new cart position.

.. warning:: This endpoint is considered experimental. It might change at any time without prior notice.

.. warning::

This endpoint is intended for advanced users. It is not designed to be used to build your own shop frontend. There is a lot that it does not or can not do, and you will need to be careful using it. It allows to bypass many of the restrictions imposed when creating a cart through the regular shop.

Specifically, this endpoint currently
- does not validate if products are only to be sold in a specific time frame
- does not validate if the event's ticket sales are already over or haven't started
- does not validate constraints on add-on products at the moment
- does not check or calculate prices but believes any prices you send
- does not prevent you from buying items that can only be bought with a voucher
- does not support file upload questions

Note that more validation might be added in the future, so please do not rely on missing validation.

You can supply the following fields of the resource:
- `cart_id` (optional, needs to end in `@api`)
- `item`
- `variation` (optional)
- `price`
- `seat` (The `seat_guid` attribute of a seat. Required when the specified `item` requires a seat, otherwise must be `null`.)
- `attendee_name` or `attendee_name_parts` (optional)
- `attendee_email` (optional)
- `subevent` (optional)
- `expires` (optional)
- `includes_tax` (optional, DEPRECATED, do not use, will be removed)
- `sales_channel` (optional)
- `voucher` (optional, expect a voucher code)
- `addons` (optional, expect a list of nested objects of cart positions)
- `bundled` (optional, expect a list of nested objects of cart positions)
- `answers`
- `question`
- `answer`
- `options`

post.description:
Creates a new order.

.. warning::

This endpoint is intended for advanced users. It is not designed to be used to build your own shop frontend, it's rather intended to import attendees from external sources etc. There is a lot that it does not or can not do, and you will need to be careful using it. It allows to bypass many of the restrictions imposed when creating an order through the regular shop.

Specifically, this endpoint currently
- does not validate if products are only to be sold in a specific time frame
- does not validate if products are only to be sold on other sales channels
- does not validate if the event's ticket sales are already over or haven't started
- does not validate the number of items per order or the number of times an item can be included in an order
- does not validate any requirements related to add-on products and does not add bundled products automatically
- does not check prices but believes any prices you send
- does not prevent you from buying items that can only be bought with a voucher
- does not calculate fees automatically
- does not allow to pass data to plugins and will therefore cause issues with some plugins like the shipping module
- does not support file upload questions
- does not support or validate memberships

You can supply the following fields of the resource:
- `code` (optional) – Only `A-Z` and `0-9`, but without `O` and `1`.
- `status` (optional) – Defaults to pending for non-free orders and paid for free orders. You can only set this to `"n"` for pending or `"p"` for paid. We will create a payment object for this order either in state `created` or in state `confirmed`, depending on this value. If you create a paid order, the `order_paid` signal will not be sent out to plugins and no email will be sent. If you want that behavior, create an unpaid order and then call the `mark_paid` API method.
- `customer` (optional) – Customer identifier or `null`
- `testmode` (optional) – Defaults to `false`
- `consume_carts` (optional) – A list of cart IDs. All cart positions with these IDs will be deleted if the order creation is successful. Any quotas or seats that become free by this operation will be credited to your order creation.
- `email` (optional)
- `locale`
- `sales_channel` (optional)
- `payment_provider` (optional) – The identifier of the payment provider set for this order. This needs to be an existing payment provider. You should use `"free"` for free orders, and we strongly advise to use `"manual"` for all orders you create as paid. This field is optional when the order status is `"n"` or the order total is zero, otherwise it is required.
- `payment_info` (optional) – You can pass a nested JSON object that will be set as the internal `info` value of the payment object that will be created. How this value is handled is up to the payment provider and you should only use this if you know the specific payment provider in detail. Please keep in mind that the payment provider will not be called to do anything about this (i.e. if you pass a bank account to a debit provider, *no* charge will be created), this is just informative in case you *handled the payment already*.
- `payment_date` (optional) – Date and time of the completion of the payment.
- `tax_rounding_mode` (optional)
- `comment` (optional)
- `custom_followup_at` (optional)
- `checkin_attention` (optional)
- `checkin_text` (optional)
- `require_approval` (optional)
- `valid_if_pending` (optional)
- `invoice_address` (optional)
- `company`
- `is_business`
- `name` or `name_parts`
- `street`
- `zipcode`
- `city`
- `country`
- `state`
- `internal_reference`
- `vat_id`
- `vat_id_validated` (optional) – If you need support for reverse charge (rarely the case), you need to check yourself if the passed VAT ID is a valid EU VAT ID. In that case, set this to `true`. Only valid VAT IDs will trigger reverse charge taxation. Don't forget to set `is_business` as well!
- `transmission_type` (optional, defaults to `email`)
- `transmission_info` (optional, see also rest-transmission-types)
- `positions`
- `positionid` (optional, see below)
- `item`
- `variation` (optional)
- `price` (optional, if set to `null` or missing the price will be computed from the given product)
- `seat` (The `seat_guid` attribute of a seat. Required when the specified `item` requires a seat, otherwise must be `null`.)
- `attendee_name` or `attendee_name_parts` (optional)
- `voucher` (optional, the `code` attribute of a valid voucher)
- `attendee_email` (optional)

- `requested_valid_from` (optional, can be set instead of `valid_from` and `valid_until` to signal a user choice for the start time that may or may not be respected)
- `use_reusable_medium` (optional, causes the new ticket to be connected to the given reusable medium, identified by its ID)
- `discount` (optional, only possible if `price` is set; attention: if this is set to not-`null` on any position, automatic calculation of discounts will not run)

If set to `true`, your `value parameter will be treated as a percentage and the fee will be calculated using that percentage and the sum of all product prices. Note that this will not include other fees and is calculated once during order generation and will not be respected automatically when the order changes later.)

post.summary: With this API call, you can instruct the system to render a set of tickets into one combined PDF file
post.description:
With this API call, you can instruct the system to render a set of tickets into one combined PDF file. To specify which tickets to render, you need to submit a list of "parts". For every part, the following fields are supported:
- `orderposition` (`integer`, required): The ID of the order position to render.
- `override_channel` (`string`, optional): The sales channel ID to be used for layout selection instead of the original channel of the order.
- `override_layout` (`integer`, optional): The ticket layout ID to be used instead of the auto-selected one.

If your input parameters validate correctly, a `202 Accepted` status code is returned. The body points you to the download URL of the result. Running a `GET` request on that result URL will yield one of the following status codes:
- `200 OK` – The export succeeded. The body will be your resulting file. Might be large!
- `409 Conflict` – Your export is still running. The body will be JSON with the structure `{"status": "running"}`. `status` can be `waiting` before the task is actually being processed. Please retry, but wait at least one second before you do.
- `410 Gone` – Running the export has failed permanently. The body will be JSON with the structure `{"status": "failed", "message": "Error message"}`
- `404 Not Found` – The export does not exist / is expired.

.. warning:: This endpoint is considered experimental. It might change at any time without prior notice.

.. note:: To avoid performance issues, a maximum number of 1000 parts is currently allowed.

checkin_attention.description: If `true`, the check-in app should show a warning that this ticket requires special attention if such a variation is being scanned.

checkin_text.description: Text that will be shown if a ticket of this type is scanned (or `null`).

require_approval.description: If `true`, orders with this variation will need to be approved by the event organizer before they can be paid.

require_membership.description: If `true`, booking this variation requires an active membership.

require_membership_hidden.description: If `true` and `require_membership` is set, this variation will be hidden from users without a valid membership.

require_membership_types.description: Internal IDs of membership types valid if `require_membership` is `true`

all_sales_channels.description: If `true` (default), the variation is available on all sales channels.

limit_sales_channels.description: List of sales channel identifiers the variation is available on if `all_sales_channels` is `false`. The item-level list takes precedence, i.e. a sales channel needs to be on both lists for the variation to be available (unless `all_sales_channels` is used).

sales_channels.description: DEPRECATED. Legacy interface, use `all_sales_channels` and `limit_sales_channels` instead.

available_from.description: The first date time at which this variation can be bought (or `null`).

available_from_mode.description: If `hide` (the default), this variation is hidden in the shop if unavailable due to the available_from setting. If `info`, the variation is visible, but can't be purchased, and a note explaining the unavailability is displayed.

available_until.description: The last date time at which this variation can be bought (or `null`).

available_until_mode.description: If `hide` (the default), this variation is hidden in the shop if unavailable due to the available_until setting. If `info`, the variation is visible, but can't be purchased, and a note explaining the unavailability is displayed.

meta_data.description: Values set for event-specific meta data parameters.

customer.description: Identifier of the customer associated with this membership (can't be changed)

testmode.description: Whether this is a test membership

membership_type.description: Internal ID of the membership type

attendee_name_parts.description: JSON representation of components of an attendee name (configuration dependent)

id.description: Internal ID of the membership type

transferable.description: Whether a membership of this type can be used by multiple persons

allow_parallel_usage.description: Whether a membership of this type can be used for multiple parallel tickets

max_usages.description: Maximum number of times a membership of this type can be used.

event.description: The slug of the parent event

status.description:
Order status, one of:

- `p` – paid
- `e` – expired
- `c` – canceled

testmode.description: If `true`, this order was created when the event was in test mode. Only orders in test mode can be deleted.

secret.description: The secret contained in the link sent to the customer

locale.description: The locale used for communication with this customer

sales_channel.description: Channel this sale was created through, such as `"web"`.

expires.description: The order will expire, if it is still pending by this time

payment_date.description: DEPRECATED AND INACCURATE Date of payment receipt

payment_provider.description: DEPRECATED AND INACCURATE Payment provider used for this order

api_meta.description: Meta data for that order. Only available through API, no guarantees on the content structure. You can use this to save references to your system.

custom_followup_at.description: Internal date for a custom follow-up action

checkin_attention.description: If `true`, the check-in app should show a warning that this ticket requires special attention if a ticket of this order is scanned.

checkin_text.description: Text that will be shown if a ticket of this order is scanned (or `null`).

last_modified.description: Last modification date of the address

is_business.description: Business or individual customers (always `false` for orders created before pretix 1.7, do not rely on it).

state.description: Customer state (ISO 3166-2 code). Only supported in AU, BR, CA, CN, MY, MX, and US.

internal_reference.description: Customer's internal reference to be printed on the invoice

vat_id_validated.description: `true`, if the VAT ID has been validated against the EU VAT service and validation was successful. This only happens in rare cases.

transmission_type.description: Transmission channel for invoice (see also rest-transmission-types). Defaults to `email`.

transmission_info.description: Transmission-channel specific information (or `null`). See also rest-transmission-types.

positions.description: List of order positions (see below). By default, only non-canceled positions are included.

id.description: Internal ID of the fee record

description.description: Human-readable string with more details (can be empty)

internal_type.description: Internal string (i.e. ID of the payment provider), can be empty

tax_rate.description: VAT rate applied for this fee

tax_rule.description: The ID of the used tax rule (or `null`)

tax_code.description: Codified reason for tax rate (or `null`), see rest-taxcodes.

canceled.description: Whether or not this fee has been canceled.

fees.description: List of fees included in the order total. By default, only non-canceled fees are included.

downloads.description: List of ticket download options for order-wise ticket downloading. This might be a multi-page PDF or a ZIP file of tickets for outputs that do not support multiple tickets natively. See also order position download options.

require_approval.description: If `true` and the order is pending, this order needs approval by an organizer before it can continue. If `true` and the order is canceled, this order has been denied by the event organizer.

valid_if_pending.description: If `true` and the order is pending, this order is still treated like a paid order for most purposes, such as check-in. This may be used e.g. for trusted customers who only need to pay after the event.

url.description: The full URL to the order confirmation page

cancellation_date.description: Time of order cancellation (or `null`). Note: Will not be set for partial cancellations and is not reliable for orders that have been cancelled, reactivated and cancelled again.

use_gift_cards.description: List of unique gift card secrets that are used to pay for this order.

local_id.description: Internal ID of this payment, starts at 1 for every order

created.description: Date and time of creation of this payment

payment_date.description: Date and time of completion of this payment (or `null`)

provider.description: Identification string of the payment provider

payment_url.description: The URL where an user can continue with the payment (or `null`)

details.description: Payment-specific information. This is a dictionary with various fields that can be different between payment providers, versions, payment states, etc. If you read this field, you always need to be able to deal with situations where values that you expect are missing. id.description: Internal ID of the order position

order.description: Order code of the order the position belongs to

positionid.description: Number of the position within the order

canceled.description: Whether or not this position has been canceled. Note that by default, only non-canceled positions are shown.

attendee_name.description: Specified attendee name for this position (or `null`)

attendee_name_parts.description: Decomposition of attendee name (i.e. given name, family name)

attendee_email.description: Specified attendee email address for this position (or `null`)

state.description: Attendee state (ISO 3166-2 code). Only supported in AU, BR, CA, CN, MY, MX, and US, otherwise `null`.

voucher.description: Internal ID of the voucher used for this position (or `null`)

voucher_budget_use.description: Amount of money discounted by the voucher, corresponding to how much of the `budget` of the voucher is consumed. Important: Do not rely on this amount to be a useful value if the position's price, product or voucher are changed *after* the order was created. Can be `null`.

tax_rate.description: VAT rate applied for this position

tax_code.description: Codified reason for tax rate (or `null`), see rest-taxcodes.

tax_rule.description: The ID of the used tax rule (or `null`)

secret.description: Secret code printed on the tickets for validation

addon_to.description: Internal ID of the position this position is an add-on for (or `null`)

subevent.description: ID of the date inside an event series this position belongs to (or `null`).

discount.description: ID of a discount that has been used during the creation of this position in some way (or `null`).

blocked.description: A list of strings, or `null`. Whenever not `null`, the ticket may not be used (e.g. for check-in).

valid_from.description: The ticket will not be valid before this time. Can be `null`.

valid_until.description: The ticket will not be valid after this time. Can be `null`.

pseudonymization_id.description: A random ID, e.g. for use in lead scanning apps

id.description: Internal ID of the check-in event

list.description: Internal ID of the check-in list

gate.description: Internal ID of the gate. Can be `null`.

device.description: Internal ID of the device. Can be `null`. Deprecated, since this ID is not otherwise used in the API and is therefore not very useful.

device_id.description: Attribute `device_id` of the device. Can be `null`.

auto_checked_in.description: Indicates if this check-in been performed automatically by the system

checkins.description: List of successful check-ins with this ticket

id.description: Internal ID of the print job

successful.description: Whether the print job successfully resulted in a print. This is not expected to be 100 % reliable information (since printer feedback is never perfect) and there is no guarantee that unsuccessful jobs will be logged.

device_id.description: Attribute `device_id` of the device that recorded the print. Can be `null`.

source.description: Source of print job, e.g. name of the app used.

print_logs.description: List of print jobs recorded e.g. by the pretix apps

question.description: Internal ID of the answered question

answer.description: Text representation of the answer (URL if answer is a file)

options.description: Internal IDs of selected option(s)s (only for choice types)

option_identifiers.description: The `identifier` fields of the selected option(s)s

id.description: Internal ID of the seat instance

zone_name.description: Name of the zone the seat is in

row_name.description: Name/number of the row the seat is in

seat_number.description: Number of the seat within the row

seat_guid.description: Identifier of the seat within the seating plan

pdf_data.description: Data object required for ticket PDF generation. By default, this field is missing. It will be added only if you add the `pdf_data=true` query parameter to your request.

local_id.description: Internal ID of this payment, starts at 1 for every order

source.description: How this refund has been created, one of `buyer`, `admin`, or `external`

created.description: Date and time of creation of this payment

comment.description: Reason for refund (shown to the customer in some cases, can be `null`).

execution_date.description: Date and time of completion of this refund (or `null`)

provider.description: Identification string of the payment provider

details.description: Refund-specific information. This is a dictionary with various fields that can be different between payment providers, versions, payment states, etc. If you read this field, you always need to be able to deal with situations where values that you expect are missing. name.description: The organizer's full name, i.e. the name of an organization or company.

slug.description: A short form of the name, used e.g. in URLs.

public_url.description: The public, customer-facing URL of the organizer, where the list of all events can be found (read-only).

plugins.description: A list of package names of the enabled plugins for this organizer. Note that most plugins are enabled on the event level (or both levels). If you remove a plugin that is also enabled on some events, it will automatically be removed from all events as well.

default.description: `true` if this is the default layout

layout.description: Dynamic layout specification. Each list element corresponds to one dynamic element of the layout. The current version of the schema in use can be found here. Submitting invalid content can lead to application errors.

item_assignments.description: Products this layout is assigned to (currently read-only)

question.description: The field label shown to the customer

help_text.description: The help text shown to the customer

type.description:
The expected type of answer. Valid options:
- `N` – number
- `S` – one-line string
- `T` – multi-line string
- `B` – boolean
- `C` – choice from a list

required.description: If `true`, the question needs to be filled out.

items.description: List of item IDs this question is assigned to.

identifier.description: An arbitrary string that can be used for matching with other sources.

ask_during_checkin.description: If `true`, this question will not be asked while buying the ticket, but will show up when redeeming the ticket instead.

show_during_checkin.description: If `true`, the answer to the question will be shown during check-in (if the check-in client supports it).

hidden.description: If `true`, the question will only be shown in the backend.

print_on_invoice.description: If `true`, the question will only be shown on invoices.

identifier.description: An arbitrary string that can be used for matching with other sources.

answer.description: The displayed value of this option

options.description: In case of question type `C` or `M`, this lists the available objects. Only writable during creation, use separate endpoint to modify this later.

valid_datetime_min.description: Minimum value for date and time questions (optional)

valid_datetime_max.description: Maximum value for date and time questions (optional)

valid_file_portrait.description: Turn on file validation for portrait photos

dependency_question.description: Internal ID of a different question. The current question will only be shown if the question given in this attribute is set to the value given in `dependency_value`. This cannot be combined with `ask_during_checkin`.

dependency_values.description: If `dependency_question` is set to a boolean question, this should be `["True"]` or `["False"]`. Otherwise, it should be a list of `identifier` values of question options.

dependency_value.description: An old version of `dependency_values` that only allows for one value. Deprecated.

identifier.description: An arbitrary string that can be used for matching with other sources.

answer.description: The displayed value of this option

name.description: The internal name of the quota

size.description: The size of the quota or `null` for unlimited

items.description: List of item IDs this quota acts on.

variations.description: List of item variation IDs this quota acts on.

subevent.description: ID of the date inside an event series this quota belongs to (or `null`).

close_when_sold_out.description: If `true`, the quota will "close" as soon as it is sold out once. Even if tickets become available again, they will not be sold unless the quota is set to open again.

closed.description: Whether the quota is currently closed (see above field).

release_after_exit.description: Whether the quota regains capacity as soon as some tickets have been scanned at an exit.

ignore_for_event_availability.description: Whether the quota is ignored when calculating the event's availability of tickets.

available.description: Whether this quota is available. Only returned if `with_availability=true` is set on the request. Do not rely on this value for critical operations, it may be slightly out of date.

available_number.description: Number of available tickets. Only returned if `with_availability=true` is set on the request. Do not rely on this value for critical operations, it may be slightly out of date. `null` means unlimited.

organizer.description: Organizer slug of the organizer who "owns" this medium.

identifier.description: Unique identifier of the medium. The format depends on the `type`.

claim_token.description: Secret token to claim ownership of the medium (or `null`)

label.description: Label to identify the medium, usually something human readable (or `null`)

active.description: Whether this medium may be used.

customer.description: Identifier of a customer account this medium belongs to.

linked_orderpositions.description: Internal IDs of tickets this medium is linked to.

linked_orderposition.description: DEPRECATED. ID of the ticket the medium is linked to, if it is linked to only one ticket. `null`, if the medium is linked to none or multiple tickets.

linked_giftcard.description: Internal ID of a gift card this medium is linked to.

info.description: Additional data, content depends on the `type`. Consider this internal to the system and don't use it for your own data.

identifier.description: Internal ID of the sales channel. For sales channel types that allow only one instance, this is the same as `type`. For sales channel types that allow multiple instances, this is always prefixed with `type.`.

label.description: Human-readable name of the sales channel

type.description: Type of the sales channel. Only channels with type `api` can currently be created through the API.

position.description: Position for sorting lists of sales channels

all_products.description: If `true`, the email is sent to buyers of all products

limit_products.description: List of product IDs, if `all_products` is not set

[**DEPRECATED**] include_pending.description: If `true`, the email is sent to pending orders. If `false`, only paid orders are considered.

restrict_to_status.description: List of order states to restrict recipients to. Valid entries are `p` for paid, `e` for expired, `c` for canceled, `n__pending_approval` for pending approval, `n__not_pending_approval_and_not_valid_if_pending` for payment pending, `n__valid_if_pending` for payment pending but already confirmed, and `n__pending_overdue` for pending with payment overdue. The default is `["p", "n__valid_if_pending"]`.

checked_in_status.description: Check-in status to restrict recipients to. Valid strings are: `null` for no filtering (default), `checked_in` for limiting to attendees that are or have been checked in, and `no_checkin` for limiting to attendees who have not checked in.

date_is_absolute.description: If `true`, the email is set at a specific point in time.

send_date.description: If `date_is_absolute` is set: Date and time to send the email.

send_offset_days.description: If `date_is_absolute` is not set, this is the number of days before/after the email is sent.

send_offset_time.description: If `date_is_absolute` is not set, this is the time of day the email is sent on the day specified by `send_offset_days`.

offset_to_event_end.description: If `true`, `send_offset_days` is relative to the event end date. Otherwise it is relative to the event start date.

offset_is_after.description: If `true`, `send_offset_days` is the number of days after the event start or end date. Otherwise it is the number of days before.

send_to.description: Can be `"orders"` if the email should be sent to customers (one email per order), `"attendees"` if the email should be sent to every attendee, or `"both"`. date. Otherwise it is relative to the event start date.

owner.description: Email address of the user who created this schedule (read-only). This address will always receive the export and the export will only contain data that this user has permission to access at the time of the export. We consider this field experimental, it's behaviour might change in the future. Note that the email address of a user can change at any time.

export_identifier.description: Identifier of the export to run, see rest-exporters

export_form_data.description: Input data for the export, format depends on the export, see rest-exporters for more details.

locale.description: Language to run the export in

mail_additional_recipients.description: Email addresses to receive the export, comma-separated (or empty string)

mail_additional_recipients_cc.description: Email addresses to receive the export in copy, comma-separated (or empty string)

mail_additional_recipients_bcc.description: Email addresses to receive the exportin blind copy, comma-separated (or empty string)

mail_subject.description: Subject to use for the email (currently no variables supported)

mail_template.description: Text to use for the email (currently no variables supported)

schedule_rrule.description: Recurrence specification to determine the days this schedule runs on in `RRULE` syntax following RFC 5545 with some restrictions. schedule_rrule_time.description: Time of day to run this on on the specified days. Will be interpreted as local time of the event for event-level exports. For organizer-level exports, the timezone is given in the field `timezone`. The export will never run before this time but it may run later.

timezone.description: Time zone to interpret the schedule in (only for organizer-level exports)

schedule_next_run.description: Next planned execution (read-only, computed by server)

error_counter.description: Number of consecutive times this export failed (read-only). After a number of failures (currently 5), the schedule no longer is executed. Changing parameters resets the value.

layout.description: JSON representation of the seating plan. These representations follow a JSON schema that currently still evolves. The version in use can be found here.

id.description: Internal ID of the tax rule

internal_name.description: An optional name that is only used in the backend

code.description: Codified reason for tax rate (or `null`), see rest-taxcodes.

price_includes_tax.description: If `true` (default), tax is assumed to be included in the specified product price

default.description: If `true` (default), this is the default tax rate for this event (there can only be one per event).

home_country.description: Merchant country (required for reverse charge), can be `null` or empty string

keep_gross_if_rate_changes.description: If `true`, changes of the tax rate based on custom rules keep the gross price constant (default is `false`)

all_events.description: Whether this team has access to all events

require_2fa.description: Whether members of this team are required to use two-factor authentication

token.description: The actual API token. Will only be sent back during token creation.

order.description: Order code the transaction was created from

positionid.description: Number of the position within the order this refers to, is `null` for transactions that refer to a fee

count.description: Number of items purchased, is negative for cancellations

code.description: The voucher code that is required to redeem the voucher

tag.description: A string that is used for grouping vouchers

comment.description: An internal comment on the voucher

subevent.description: ID of the date inside an event series this voucher belongs to (or `null`).

all_addons_included.description: If set to `true`, all add-on products for the product purchased with this voucher are included in the base price.

all_bundles_included.description: If set to `true`, all bundled products for the product purchased with this voucher are added without their designated price.

budget.description: The budget a voucher is allowed to consume before being used up (or `null`)

budget_used.description: The amount of budget the voucher has already used up.
